hints: Look at what all four bullet points have in common. They are all about food, drinking water, and washing hands, not about insects, coughing, or the air.
Ask yourself which disease spreads by the faecal-oral route in contaminated food and water, so that cooking, peeling, boiling water and handwashing would break its transmission.
walkthrough:
**Spot the pattern in the advice**

All four tips are about hygiene of what goes into your mouth. Cook food, peel fruit, boil drinking water, wash hands with clean water.

This tells us we are trying to stop a pathogen entering through the gut.

**Link advice to transmission route**

Cooking and boiling kill pathogens with heat. Peeling and handwashing remove pathogens from surfaces.

This is classic protection against faecal-oral transmission, where faeces contaminate water, food or hands.

**Match to the disease list**

Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae spread in contaminated water and food. The advice directly blocks it.

Malaria is mosquito-borne, measles and tuberculosis are airborne, so food and water hygiene would not protect against them.

options.A: Correct, cholera spreads by ingesting contaminated water or food, so cooking, peeling, boiling water and handwashing directly prevent infection.
options.B: False, malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito, so protection needs mosquito nets and repellents, not food hygiene.
options.C: False, measles is a highly infectious airborne virus spread in droplets, so boiling water and cooking food will not stop it.
options.D: False, tuberculosis is mainly an airborne bacterial infection spread by coughing, so clean food and water do not block its main route.
